exceptions.rationale: age 0.12.1 requires rsa 0.9 for SSH-RSA recipient compatibility and no patched stable rsa release is available. gitforgeops only parses RSA public keys and encrypts locally; it never accepts an RSA private key or exposes RSA signing/decryption timing to a remote observer.
compensating_controls: RSA use is limited to local encryption with public recipient material; the vulnerable private-key operations are unreachable.
age rejects SSH-RSA recipient keys smaller than 2048 bits, and gitforgeops parses public recipient material only.

CI pins the age feature declaration and the gitforgeops -> age -> rsa dependency path, and rejects unreviewed `age::` references under `src/` outside the encryption-only delivery module. This is a syntactic source scan; it does not cover tests, build scripts, or re-exports.
The exact package, version, and advisory must match this policy and CI rejects stale or expired exceptions.

exceptions.rationale: Pending owner acceptance: time-boxed risk acceptance, not an owner-approved exception until the owner merges it. crypto-bigint 0.5.5 has timing variability in operations meant to be constant-time; it is fixed only in >= 0.7.6 and there is no patched 0.5.x. age 0.12.1 (latest) requires p256 ^0.13 and hpke 0.12 for its native P-256 tag recipients, so the crate cannot be upgraded away. gitforgeops only encrypts to SSH recipients (ssh-ed25519 / ssh-rsa) parsed from public keys. It never constructs an age P-256 tag recipient or any age identity, and age rejects ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 SSH keys, so no p256 or crypto-bigint arithmetic runs in gitforgeops, on secret or public values.
affected_call_paths: gitforgeops -> age 0.12.1 / age-core 0.12.0 -> hpke 0.12.0 (p256 feature) -> p256 0.13.2 -> elliptic-curve 0.13.8 -> crypto-bigint 0.5.5
src/secrets/delivery.rs: age::ssh::Recipient public-key encryption only (no P-256 recipient, no identity, no decryption)
compensating_controls: The age API boundary is limited to SSH-recipient encryption (age::ssh::Recipient, age::Encryptor, the age::Recipient trait and armor) in src/secrets/delivery.rs. That excludes the native P-256 tag/tagpq recipients and every identity or decryptor that would run P-256 ECDH or HPKE with a secret scalar.

CI pins the age 0.12 feature declaration (exactly ssh and armor) and the complete crypto-bigint 0.5 dependency graph to gitforgeops -> age 0.12 -> p256 0.13 / hpke 0.12. A direct p256 dependency or a RustCrypto JWT signing backend would therefore fail the gate. The age scan is a syntactic source check; it does not cover tests, build scripts, or re-exports.
jsonwebtoken uses its aws_lc_rs provider with default features disabled, so it does not pull in p256 0.13.
The exact package, version, and advisory must match this policy, and CI rejects stale or expired exceptions.
